en.L: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day, and arranged [the] battle [line] against Gibeah as time by time.
en.B: On the third day the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites and drew up their battle lines against Gibeah as they had done before.
en.R: On the third day the Israelites went up to fight the men of Benjamin. They took their positions for battle at Gibeah just as they had done the other times.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakapanda juu ya wana wa Benyamini siku ya tatu, wakapanga [safu za vita] juu ya Gibea kama mara zile nyingine.
sw.B: Siku ya tatu Waisraeli walipanda kupigana na Wabenyamini, wakapanga safu zao za vita dhidi ya Gibea kama walivyofanya mara zile nyingine.
sw.R: Siku ya tatu Waisraeli walipanda kupigana na watu wa Benyamini. Walichukua nafasi zao za vita huko Gibea kama walivyofanya mara zile nyingine.

es.L: Y subieron los hijos de Israel contra los hijos de Benjamín al tercer día, y ordenaron [la batalla] contra Guibeá como las otras veces.
es.B: Al tercer día los israelitas subieron contra los benjamitas y se pusieron en orden de batalla frente a Guibeá, como las otras veces.
es.R: Al tercer día los israelitas subieron a pelear contra los hombres de Benjamín. Tomaron sus posiciones para la batalla en Guibeá, igual que las otras veces.

decisions.choice: as time by time: as on the other occasions
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as before", the same way they had done twice already. It is part of the plan: Benjamin is to think this is one more battle like the others (verse 32).

decisions.choice: arranged
decisions.reason: As in verse 20: drew up the army for battle; here the word "battle" is understood.

decisions.choice: arranged [the] battle [line] / drew up their battle lines / took their positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20. Literal brackets "the battle line", which the Hebrew leaves understood here.

source.text: וַיֵּצְא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִן֙ לִקְרַ֣את הָעָ֔ם הָנְתְּק֖וּ מִן־הָעִ֑יר וַיָּחֵ֡לּוּ לְהַכּוֹת֩ מֵהָעָ֨ם חֲלָלִ֜ים כְּפַ֣עַם׀בְּפַ֗עַם בַּֽמְסִלּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַחַ֜ת עֹלָ֣ה בֵֽית־אֵ֗ל וְאַחַ֤ת גִּבְעָ֨תָה֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] sons of Benjamin to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike from the people slain, as time by time, on the highways, of which one goes up [to] Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty man in Israel.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people; they were drawn away from the city. And they began to strike [some] of the people, slain as time by time, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men in Israel.
en.B: The Benjaminites came out to meet the army and were drawn away from the town. As before, they began to strike down some of the troops on the roads, one leading up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, in the open country. They killed about thirty men of Israel.
en.R: The men of Benjamin came out to fight the army, and the Israelites led them away from the town. As before, the men of Benjamin began killing some of the soldiers in the open country along the roads. One road went to Bethel and the other to Gibeah. They killed about thirty men of Israel.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakatoka kuwalaki watu; wakavutwa mbali na mji. Wakaanza kuwapiga [baadhi] ya watu, waliouawa kama mara zile nyingine, katika njia kuu, moja yao ipandayo Betheli na moja Gibea mashambani, watu wapata thelathini katika Israeli.
sw.B: Wabenyamini walitoka kulilaki jeshi, wakavutwa mbali na mji. Kama mara zile nyingine, walianza kuwaua baadhi ya askari katika njia kuu, moja ikipanda Betheli na nyingine Gibea, huko mashambani. Waliwaua watu wapata thelathini wa Israeli.
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini walitoka kupigana na jeshi, na Waisraeli wakawavuta mbali na mji. Kama mara zile nyingine, watu wa Benyamini walianza kuwaua baadhi ya askari mashambani kando ya njia. Njia moja ilikwenda Betheli na nyingine Gibea. Waliwaua watu wapata thelathini wa Israeli.

es.L: Y salieron los hijos de Benjamín al encuentro del pueblo; fueron alejados de la ciudad. Y comenzaron a herir [a algunos] del pueblo, muertos como las otras veces, en los caminos, uno de los cuales sube a Betel y otro a Guibeá en el campo, unos treinta hombres de Israel.
es.B: Los benjamitas salieron al encuentro del ejército y se dejaron alejar de la ciudad. Como antes, comenzaron a abatir a algunos de la tropa en los caminos, uno que sube a Betel y otro a Guibeá, en campo abierto. Mataron a unos treinta hombres de Israel.
es.R: Los hombres de Benjamín salieron a pelear contra el ejército, y los israelitas los alejaron del pueblo. Como antes, los de Benjamín comenzaron a matar a algunos soldados en campo abierto, a lo largo de los caminos. Un camino iba a Betel y el otro a Guibeá. Mataron a unos treinta hombres de Israel.

decisions.choice: they were drawn away from the city: pulled away by the tribes' pretended retreat
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: the Benjaminites were led away from Gibeah without knowing it. Verse 32 tells how the tribes planned it, and Joshua 8:16 uses the same verb of the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: Gibeah in the field: as the Hebrew has it, though Gibeah is the city they left
decisions.reason: The Benjaminites have just left Gibeah, so a road "to Gibeah" is surprising. It may mean a road back toward Gibeah across open country. It may also be a slip for Gibeon, a town to the west whose name is very like it in Hebrew; the Hebrew text has Gibeah.

decisions.choice: highways: the main roads
decisions.reason: The word means a built-up road or highway. Fighting on the roads in open country, away from the town, was what the tribes wanted (verse 32).

decisions.choice: They killed about thirty men of Israel.
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the number in its own sentence; in the Hebrew it comes at the end of the long description of the roads.

decisions.choice: the Israelites led them
decisions.reason: Readable makes the passive verb active and says who drew them away (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֔ן נִגָּפִ֥ים הֵ֛ם לְפָנֵ֖ינוּ כְּבָרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וּבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָמְר֗וּ נָנ֨וּסָה֙ וּֽנְתַקְּנֻ֔הוּ מִן־הָעִ֖יר אֶל־הַֽמְסִלּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] sons of Benjamin, They are struck down before us as at the first. And [the] sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are struck down before us as at the first." But the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw him away from the city to the highways."
en.B: The Benjaminites said, "They are being beaten by us as they were before." But the Israelites had said, "Let us run away and draw them out from the town onto the roads."
en.R: The men of Benjamin said, "We are beating them, just as we did before." But the Israelites had planned this. They had said, "Let us run away, so that we can lead them away from the town and onto the roads."

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakasema, "Wamepigwa mbele yetu kama mara ya kwanza." Lakini wana wa Israeli wakasema, "Na tukimbie, tumvute mbali na mji mpaka kwenye njia kuu."
sw.B: Wabenyamini walisema, "Wanashindwa mbele yetu kama walivyoshindwa mwanzoni." Lakini Waisraeli walikuwa wamesema, "Tukimbie, tuwavute kutoka mjini mpaka kwenye njia kuu."
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini walisema, "Tunawashinda, kama tulivyofanya mwanzoni." Lakini Waisraeli walikuwa wamepanga jambo hili. Walikuwa wamesema, "Tukimbie, ili tuwavute mbali na mji mpaka kwenye njia."

es.L: Y dijeron los hijos de Benjamín: «Son derrotados delante de nosotros como al principio». Pero los hijos de Israel dijeron: «Huyamos y alejémoslo de la ciudad hacia los caminos».
es.B: Los benjamitas decían: «Los estamos derrotando como la primera vez». Pero los israelitas habían dicho: «Huyamos y saquémoslos de la ciudad hacia los caminos».
es.R: Los hombres de Benjamín decían: «Les estamos ganando, igual que antes». Pero los israelitas lo habían planeado así. Habían dicho: «Huyamos, para alejarlos del pueblo y llevarlos a los caminos».

decisions.choice: and the sons of Israel said: the plan made before the battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two sayings side by side. The tribes' words are the plan they had made beforehand, now told to show why Benjamin was wrong.

decisions.choice: struck down: defeated
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an army beaten in battle (verse 36; 1 Samuel 4:2).

decisions.choice: had said (B); had planned this. They had said (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the tribes' words came before, as the plan (m1).

source.text: וְכֹ֣ל׀אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל קָ֚מוּ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ וַיַּעַרְכ֖וּ בְּבַ֣עַל תָּמָ֑ר וְאֹרֵ֧ב יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵגִ֥יחַ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ מִמַּֽעֲרֵה־גָֽבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And every man of Israel rose from his place and arranged at Baal-tamar, and [the] ambush of Israel [was] bursting out from its place, from [the] open place of Geba.

en.L: And all the men of Israel rose from their place and arranged [the battle line] at Baal-tamar, and the ambush of Israel was bursting out from its place, from the open place of Geba.
en.B: All the men of Israel rose up from where they were and drew up their battle lines at Baal-tamar, while the men of Israel in ambush burst out from their position west of Geba.
en.R: The main Israelite army left its position and took its positions for battle at Baal-tamar. At the same time the soldiers who were hiding west of Geba rushed out from their hiding place.

sw.L: Nao watu wote wa Israeli wakainuka kutoka mahali pao, wakapanga [safu za vita] huko Baal-tamari, nao waviziaji wa Israeli walikuwa wakitoka kwa kasi mahali pao, kutoka uwanda wa Geba.
sw.B: Watu wote wa Israeli waliinuka kutoka mahali walipokuwa, wakapanga safu zao za vita huko Baal-tamari, wakati watu wa Israeli waliokuwa wakivizia walitoka kwa kasi mahali pao upande wa magharibi wa Geba.
sw.R: Jeshi kuu la Israeli liliacha mahali pake, likachukua nafasi zake za vita huko Baal-tamari. Wakati huo huo askari waliokuwa wamejificha magharibi ya Geba walitoka kwa kasi katika maficho yao.

es.L: Y todos los hombres de Israel se levantaron de su lugar y se ordenaron [en batalla] en Baal-tamar, y la emboscada de Israel irrumpía de su lugar, del claro de Geba.
es.B: Todos los hombres de Israel se levantaron de donde estaban y se pusieron en orden de batalla en Baal-tamar, mientras los israelitas emboscados irrumpían desde su posición al oeste de Geba.
es.R: El grueso del ejército israelita dejó su lugar y tomó sus posiciones para la batalla en Baal-tamar. Al mismo tiempo, los soldados que estaban escondidos al oeste de Geba salieron corriendo de su escondite.

decisions.choice: Baal-tamar: a place near Gibeah, not known today
decisions.reason: The name means "lord of the palm tree". Its site is not known, but it lay near Gibeah, where the main army turned to fight.

decisions.choice: the open place of Geba: a clearing near Geba, or west of Geba
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is rare and may mean a bare or open place. The Greek translation and the Latin read it as "west of" and some read "Gibeah" for "Geba". The ambush came out from an open area beside one of these two towns.

decisions.choice: was bursting out: at the same moment
decisions.reason: The verb form describes action going on at the same time as the main army's turn. As the army turned to face Benjamin, the ambush rushed out behind them.

decisions.choice: west of Geba
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the reading "west of" as the most likely sense of the rare word (m2); Literal keeps "the open place". Readable also says "west".

decisions.choice: arranged [the battle line] / drew up their battle lines / took its positions for battle
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

source.text: וַיָּבֹאוּ֩ מִנֶּ֨גֶד לַגִּבְעָ֜ה עֲשֶׂרֶת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אִ֤ישׁ בָּחוּר֙ מִכָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה כָּבֵ֑דָה וְהֵם֙ לֹ֣א יָדְע֔וּ כִּֽי־נֹגַ֥עַת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הָרָעָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came from before the Gibeah ten thousand man chosen from all Israel, and the battle [was] heavy; and they did not know that touching upon them [was] the disaster.

en.L: And there came from opposite Gibeah 10,000 chosen men from all Israel, and the battle was heavy; and they did not know that the disaster was touching them.
en.B: Then 10,000 chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the fighting was fierce. The Benjaminites did not realize that disaster was about to strike them.
en.R: Then 10,000 of Israel's best soldiers attacked Gibeah. The fighting was hard. The men of Benjamin did not know that disaster was about to fall on them.

sw.L: Wakaja kutoka mkabala na Gibea watu 10,000 waliochaguliwa kutoka Israeli wote, na vita vikawa vikali; wala hawakujua ya kuwa maafa yalikuwa yakiwagusa.
sw.B: Kisha watu 10,000 waliochaguliwa kutoka Israeli wote waliishambulia Gibea, na mapigano yakawa makali. Wabenyamini hawakutambua kwamba maafa yalikuwa karibu kuwapata.
sw.R: Kisha askari 10,000 bora wa Israeli waliishambulia Gibea. Mapigano yalikuwa makali. Watu wa Benyamini hawakujua kwamba maafa yalikuwa karibu kuwaangukia.

es.L: Y vinieron frente a Guibeá 10 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel, y la batalla fue dura; y ellos no sabían que la desgracia los alcanzaba.
es.B: Entonces 10 000 hombres escogidos de todo Israel atacaron Guibeá, y la lucha fue encarnizada. Los benjamitas no se dieron cuenta de que la desgracia estaba a punto de caer sobre ellos.
es.R: Entonces 10 000 de los mejores soldados de Israel atacaron Guibeá. La lucha fue dura. Los hombres de Benjamín no sabían que la desgracia estaba a punto de caer sobre ellos.

decisions.choice: came from before Gibeah: came at Gibeah from the front, or from opposite it
decisions.reason: The words "from before" may mean the ambush came from the side facing Gibeah, or that the 10,000 attacked the town head on. Either way it is the force that would take Gibeah.

decisions.choice: they did not know: the Benjaminites
decisions.reason: "They" are the men of Benjamin, still fighting on the roads, who did not see the ambush taking their town behind them (verses 40-41).

decisions.choice: the disaster touching them: ruin about to reach them
decisions.reason: The word is the same one used for the "evil" of Gibeah in verses 3, 12 and 13. The evil that Benjamin refused to remove now comes upon them as disaster.

decisions.choice: The Benjaminites / The men of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are (m2).

source.text: וַיִּגֹּ֨ף יְהוָ֥ה׀אֶֽת־בִּנְיָמִן֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּשְׁחִיתוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בְּבִנְיָמִן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה אֶ֛לֶף וּמֵאָ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה שֹׁ֥לֵף חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And struck Yahweh Benjamin before Israel, and destroyed [the] sons of Israel in Benjamin on the day the that twenty and five thousand and a hundred man; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed in Benjamin on that day 25,100 men; all these [were] drawing [the] sword.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} defeated Benjamin before Israel, and that day the Israelites cut down 25,100 men of Benjamin, all of them armed with swords.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Israel victory over Benjamin. That day the Israelites killed 25,100 of Benjamin's soldiers, all armed with swords.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampiga Benyamini mbele ya Israeli, na wana wa Israeli wakaangamiza katika Benyamini siku hiyo watu 25,100; hawa wote [walikuwa] wenye kufuta upanga.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimshinda Benyamini mbele ya Israeli, na siku hiyo Waisraeli waliwaua watu 25,100 wa Benyamini, wote wakiwa na panga.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa Israeli ushindi juu ya Benyamini. Siku hiyo Waisraeli waliwaua askari 25,100 wa Benyamini, wote wenye panga.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hirió a Benjamín delante de Israel, y los hijos de Israel destruyeron en Benjamín aquel día 25 100 hombres; todos estos sacaban espada.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} derrotó a Benjamín delante de Israel, y aquel día los israelitas abatieron a 25 100 hombres de Benjamín, todos ellos armados de espada.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Israel la victoria sobre Benjamín. Aquel día los israelitas mataron a 25 100 soldados de Benjamín, todos armados con espadas.

decisions.choice: the LORD struck Benjamin: the victory is God's
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Benjamin used of Israel in verse 32. Now it is the LORD who strikes, as he promised in verse 28. The battle is told as his act first, and only then as Israel's.

decisions.choice: 25,100: a summary of the whole battle, told before the details
decisions.reason: This verse gives the result of the day. Verses 36-46 go back and tell how the battle went, step by step, ending with a round total of 25,000 (verse 46). On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: defeated Benjamin before Israel (B); gave Israel victory over Benjamin (R)
decisions.reason: "Struck before" means defeated in front of, or for, Israel. Readable says plainly that God gave the victory.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִ֖ן כִּ֣י נִגָּ֑פוּ וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל מָקוֹם֙ לְבִנְיָמִ֔ן כִּ֤י בָֽטְחוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֹרֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁר שָׂ֖מוּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw [the] sons of Benjamin that they were struck down. And gave [the] men of Israel place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush which they had set against the Gibeah.

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck down. And the men of Israel gave place to Benjamin, for they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.
en.B: Then the Benjaminites saw that they were beaten. The men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they were counting on the ambush they had set against Gibeah.
en.R: Then the men of Benjamin saw that they had lost. The Israelites had pulled back from them on purpose, because they were counting on the soldiers they had hidden near Gibeah.

sw.L: Nao wana wa Benyamini wakaona ya kuwa wamepigwa. Na watu wa Israeli walikuwa wamempa Benyamini nafasi, kwa maana waliwategemea wale waviziaji waliowaweka juu ya Gibea.
sw.B: Kisha Wabenyamini waliona kwamba wameshindwa. Watu wa Israeli walikuwa wamerudi nyuma mbele ya Benyamini, kwa sababu waliwategemea watu wa kuvizia waliowaweka dhidi ya Gibea.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Benyamini waliona kwamba wameshindwa. Waisraeli walikuwa wamerudi nyuma mbele yao kwa makusudi, kwa sababu waliwategemea askari waliokuwa wamewaficha karibu na Gibea.

es.L: Y vieron los hijos de Benjamín que estaban derrotados. Y los hombres de Israel dieron lugar a Benjamín, porque confiaban en la emboscada que habían puesto contra Guibeá.
es.B: Entonces los benjamitas vieron que estaban derrotados. Los hombres de Israel habían cedido terreno ante Benjamín, porque contaban con la emboscada que habían puesto contra Guibeá.
es.R: Entonces los hombres de Benjamín vieron que habían perdido. Los israelitas se habían retirado a propósito, porque contaban con los soldados que habían escondido cerca de Guibeá.

decisions.choice: Benjamin saw that they were struck down: the end of the battle, told first
decisions.reason: The first sentence gives the end, when the Benjaminites saw they had lost (verse 41). The rest of the verse goes back to tell how it came about, starting with Israel's pretended retreat.

decisions.choice: gave place: gave way, pulled back
decisions.reason: To give place is to yield ground, here on purpose, so that the Benjaminites would follow them away from Gibeah (verse 32).

decisions.choice: trusted in the ambush: relied on it
decisions.reason: The verb means to trust or rely on. The tribes could fall back because they knew the hidden men would take the town behind the Benjaminites.

decisions.choice: had given ground (B); had pulled back ... on purpose (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show by the tense that this happened before Benjamin saw its defeat (m1). Readable says why they pulled back.

source.text: וְהָאֹרֵ֣ב הֵחִ֔ישׁוּ וַֽיִּפְשְׁט֖וּ אֶל־הַגִּבְעָ֑ה וַיִּמְשֹׁךְ֙ הָאֹרֵ֔ב וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־כָּל־הָעִ֖יר לְפִי־חָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And the ambush hurried and rushed against the Gibeah, and moved on the ambush and struck all the city to [the] mouth of [the] sword.

en.L: And the ambush hurried and rushed against Gibeah, and the ambush moved on and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
en.B: The men in ambush moved quickly and rushed into Gibeah. They spread out and struck down the whole town with the sword.
en.R: The soldiers who had been hiding rushed quickly into Gibeah. They spread through the town and killed everyone in it with their swords.

sw.L: Nao waviziaji wakafanya haraka, wakaishambulia Gibea, nao waviziaji wakaenea, wakaupiga mji wote kwa makali ya upanga.
sw.B: Watu waliokuwa wakivizia walikwenda upesi, wakaingia Gibea kwa kasi. Walienea mjini, wakawaua watu wote wa mji kwa upanga.
sw.R: Askari waliokuwa wamejificha waliingia Gibea upesi. Walienea katika mji wote, wakamwua kila mtu aliyekuwamo kwa panga zao.

es.L: Y la emboscada se apresuró y se lanzó contra Guibeá, y la emboscada avanzó e hirió a toda la ciudad a filo de espada.
es.B: Los emboscados se movieron con rapidez y se lanzaron sobre Guibeá. Se desplegaron e hirieron a espada a toda la ciudad.
es.R: Los soldados que habían estado escondidos entraron corriendo en Guibeá. Se extendieron por el pueblo y mataron a todos con sus espadas.

decisions.choice: moved on: spread out through the town
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw out or march on. Here the ambush, once inside, spreads through Gibeah. The same verb is used of an army moving forward in 4:6.

decisions.choice: struck the whole city with the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: As at 1:8: they killed the people of the town. The town's fighting men were away on the roads, so those killed were chiefly those left inside.

decisions.choice: the men in ambush (B); the soldiers who had been hiding (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one word, "the ambush", for the hidden men. Balanced and Readable speak of the men.

source.text: וְהַמּוֹעֵ֗ד הָיָ֛ה לְאִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִם־הָאֹרֵ֑ב הֶ֕רֶב לְהַעֲלוֹתָ֛ם מַשְׂאַ֥ת הֶעָשָׁ֖ן מִן־הָעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the appointed sign was to [the] men of Israel with the ambush: make great their causing to go up [a] rising of the smoke from the city.

en.L: And the appointed sign that the men of Israel had with the ambush was [this]: make great their sending up of a rising of smoke from the city.
en.B: The men of Israel had agreed on a signal with the men in ambush: they were to send up a great cloud of smoke from the town.
en.R: The Israelite army and the hidden soldiers had agreed on a signal. When the soldiers had taken the town, they would make a large cloud of smoke rise from it.

sw.L: Na ishara iliyoagwa kati ya watu wa Israeli na waviziaji ilikuwa [hii]: wapandishe sana wingu la moshi kutoka mjini.
sw.B: Watu wa Israeli walikuwa wamekubaliana na wale waliokuwa wakivizia ishara hii: wangepandisha wingu kubwa la moshi kutoka mjini.
sw.R: Jeshi la Israeli na wale askari waliojificha walikuwa wamekubaliana ishara. Askari hao wakishauteka mji, wangefanya wingu kubwa la moshi lipande kutoka humo.

es.L: Y la señal convenida que [tenían] los hombres de Israel con la emboscada [era esta]: que hicieran subir de la ciudad una gran columna de humo.
es.B: Los hombres de Israel habían acordado una señal con los emboscados: harían subir de la ciudad una gran nube de humo.
es.R: El ejército israelita y los soldados escondidos habían acordado una señal. Cuando los soldados tomaran el pueblo, harían subir de él una gran nube de humo.

decisions.choice: the appointed sign: a signal agreed beforehand
decisions.reason: The word means an appointed time or place, here an agreed signal. The smoke would tell the main army to turn and fight (verses 39-40), as the smoke of Ai did in Joshua 8:20-21.

decisions.choice: make great their sending up: the Hebrew is hard to read here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads awkwardly, as if "make great" were a command inside the description of the sign. It most likely means they were to make a great column of smoke rise. A word may have dropped out of the text.

decisions.choice: a rising of smoke: a column of smoke
decisions.reason: The word for "rising" is used of a signal fire or column of smoke that goes up (Jeremiah 6:1). Verse 40 calls it "a pillar of smoke".

decisions.choice: When the soldiers had taken the town
decisions.reason: Readable says when the signal was to be given, as verses 37 and 40 show.

source.text: וַיַּהֲפֹ֥ךְ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וּבִנְיָמִ֡ן הֵחֵל֩ לְהַכּ֨וֹת חֲלָלִ֤ים בְּאִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ אַךְ֩ נִגּ֨וֹף נִגָּ֥ף הוּא֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כַּמִּלְחָמָ֖ה הָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned [the] men of Israel in the battle. And Benjamin had begun to strike slain among [the] men of Israel, about thirty man, for they said, Surely struck down, struck down [is] he before us, as the battle the first.

en.L: And the men of Israel turned in the battle. And Benjamin had begun to strike [some] slain among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, "Surely he is utterly struck down before us, as [in] the first battle."
en.B: Then the men of Israel turned around in the battle. Benjamin had already started cutting down the men of Israel and had killed about thirty of them, and they said, "They are surely beaten by us, as in the first battle."
en.R: Then the men of Israel turned back to fight. The men of Benjamin had already begun to kill some of them, about thirty men. They said, "We are surely beating them, just as we did in the first battle."

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakageuka vitani. Naye Benyamini alikuwa ameanza kuwapiga [baadhi] ya watu wa Israeli, watu wapata thelathini, kwa maana walisema, "Hakika amepigwa, amepigwa mbele yetu, kama [katika] vita vya kwanza."
sw.B: Kisha watu wa Israeli waligeuka vitani. Benyamini alikuwa ameshaanza kuwaua watu wa Israeli, akawaua wapata thelathini, wakasema, "Hakika wanashindwa mbele yetu kama katika vita vya kwanza."
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Israeli waligeuka kupigana. Watu wa Benyamini walikuwa wameshaanza kuwaua baadhi yao, watu wapata thelathini. Walisema, "Hakika tunawashinda, kama tulivyofanya katika vita vya kwanza."

es.L: Y los hombres de Israel se volvieron en la batalla. Y Benjamín había comenzado a herir de muerte entre los hombres de Israel a unos treinta hombres, porque decían: «Ciertamente está del todo derrotado delante de nosotros, como en la primera batalla».
es.B: Entonces los hombres de Israel dieron la vuelta en la batalla. Benjamín ya había empezado a abatir a los hombres de Israel y había matado a unos treinta, y decían: «Seguro que los estamos derrotando, como en la primera batalla».
es.R: Entonces los hombres de Israel se dieron la vuelta para pelear. Los hombres de Benjamín ya habían empezado a matar a algunos de ellos, unos treinta hombres. Decían: «Seguro que les estamos ganando, igual que en la primera batalla».

decisions.choice: the men of Israel turned in the battle: they stopped retreating and faced Benjamin
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn round. Up to now the tribes had been pretending to flee; at the signal they turned and fought. Verse 41 tells the same turn again, at the moment Benjamin saw the smoke.

decisions.choice: Benjamin had begun to strike: what happened before the turn, as in verse 31
decisions.reason: This repeats verses 31-32 to explain why Benjamin pressed on: they had killed about thirty men and believed they were winning again.

decisions.choice: surely struck down, struck down: the doubled verb for certainty
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats a verb to stress it. The Benjaminites are sure the tribes are beaten.

decisions.choice: They are surely beaten by us (B); We are surely beating them (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he" for Israel as one man. Balanced and Readable say "they" or "them".

source.text: וְהַמַּשְׂאֵ֗ת הֵחֵ֛לָּה לַעֲל֥וֹת מִן־הָעִ֖יר עַמּ֣וּד עָשָׁ֑ן וַיִּ֤פֶן בִּנְיָמִן֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְהִנֵּ֛ה עָלָ֥ה כְלִיל־הָעִ֖יר הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the rising began to go up from the city, [a] pillar of smoke, and turned Benjamin behind him, and look, went up [the] whole of the city to the heavens.

en.L: And the rising began to go up from the city, a pillar of smoke, and Benjamin turned behind him, and look, the whole of the city was going up to the heavens.
en.B: But when the signal began to rise from the town in a column of smoke, the Benjaminites looked behind them, and there was the whole town going up in smoke to the sky.
en.R: Then the signal of smoke began to rise from the town like a pillar. The men of Benjamin looked back and saw the whole town burning, with smoke rising up to the sky.

sw.L: Na wingu likaanza kupanda kutoka mjini, nguzo ya moshi, naye Benyamini akatazama nyuma yake, na tazama, mji wote ulikuwa ukipanda mbinguni.
sw.B: Lakini ishara ilipoanza kupanda kutoka mjini kama nguzo ya moshi, Wabenyamini walitazama nyuma yao, na tazama, mji wote ulikuwa ukipanda angani kwa moshi.
sw.R: Kisha ishara ya moshi ilianza kupanda kutoka mjini kama nguzo. Watu wa Benyamini walitazama nyuma, wakaona mji wote ukiungua, moshi ukipanda mpaka angani.

es.L: Y la columna comenzó a subir de la ciudad, una columna de humo, y Benjamín miró tras de sí, y he aquí, toda la ciudad subía hacia los cielos.
es.B: Pero cuando la señal comenzó a subir de la ciudad en una columna de humo, los benjamitas miraron hacia atrás, y vieron que toda la ciudad subía en humo hacia el cielo.
es.R: Entonces la señal de humo comenzó a subir del pueblo como una columna. Los hombres de Benjamín miraron hacia atrás y vieron todo el pueblo ardiendo, con el humo subiendo hasta el cielo.

decisions.choice: the whole of the city: the town going up as a whole offering
decisions.reason: The word for "whole" is also used of an offering burned completely on the altar. The law commands that a town in Israel that turns to other gods be burned as a whole offering to the LORD (Deuteronomy 13:17); Gibeah is treated like such a town. The same picture is used of Ai (Joshua 8:20).

decisions.choice: turned behind him, and look: the story shows what the Benjaminites saw
decisions.reason: "Look" puts the reader where the Benjaminites stood, turning to see their town in smoke.

decisions.choice: the signal ... in a column of smoke (B); the signal of smoke ... like a pillar (R)
decisions.reason: "The rising" is the agreed signal of verse 38, so Balanced and Readable call it the signal.

source.text: וְאִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הָפַ֔ךְ וַיִּבָּהֵ֖ל אִ֣ישׁ בִּנְיָמִ֑ן כִּ֣י רָאָ֔ה כִּֽי־נָגְעָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו הָרָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] men of Israel turned, and were terrified [the] men of Benjamin, for he saw that had touched upon him the disaster.

en.L: And the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that the disaster had touched them.
en.B: Then the men of Israel turned to fight, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, because they saw that disaster had come upon them.
en.R: Then the men of Israel turned to attack, and the men of Benjamin were terrified. They saw that disaster had come upon them.

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakageuka, nao watu wa Benyamini wakafadhaika, kwa maana waliona ya kuwa maafa yamewagusa.
sw.B: Kisha watu wa Israeli waligeuka kupigana, na watu wa Benyamini wakaogopa sana, kwa sababu waliona kwamba maafa yamewapata.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Israeli waligeuka kuwashambulia, na watu wa Benyamini wakaogopa sana. Waliona kwamba maafa yamewapata.

es.L: Y los hombres de Israel se volvieron, y los hombres de Benjamín se aterraron, porque vieron que la desgracia los había alcanzado.
es.B: Entonces los hombres de Israel se volvieron para pelear, y los hombres de Benjamín se llenaron de terror, porque vieron que la desgracia había caído sobre ellos.
es.R: Entonces los hombres de Israel se volvieron para atacar, y los hombres de Benjamín se aterrorizaron. Vieron que la desgracia había caído sobre ellos.

decisions.choice: the disaster had touched them: what they did not know in verse 34
decisions.reason: Verse 34 said they did not know that disaster was about to reach them. Now they see it. The word is the one for the "evil" of Gibeah (verses 3, 12-13).

decisions.choice: terrified: struck with sudden fear and confusion
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dismayed or thrown into panic, as an army is when it sees it is lost (1 Samuel 28:21).

decisions.choice: they ... them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he saw" and "him" for the men of Benjamin as one body. Even Literal says "they" and "them" here, since English cannot use "he" after "the men of Benjamin".

source.text: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ לִפְנֵ֨י אִ֤ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְהַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה הִדְבִּיקָ֑תְהוּ וַאֲשֶׁר֙ מֵהֶ֣עָרִ֔ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֥ים אוֹת֖וֹ בְּתוֹכֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned before [the] men of Israel to [the] way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook him, and [those] who [were] from the cities [were] destroying him in its midst.

en.L: And they turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and those who [were] from the cities were destroying them in its midst.
en.B: So they turned and fled from the men of Israel toward the wilderness, but they could not escape the fighting, and those who came out of the towns cut them down in the middle of it.
en.R: So they ran from the men of Israel toward the wilderness. But they could not escape the battle. Israelite soldiers came out of the towns and killed them there between the two armies.

sw.L: Nao wakageuka mbele ya watu wa Israeli kuelekea njia ya nyika, lakini vita vikawafikia, nao waliotoka mijini wakawaangamiza katikati yake.
sw.B: Basi waligeuka wakawakimbia watu wa Israeli kuelekea nyikani, lakini hawakuweza kuyaepuka mapigano, na wale waliotoka mijini wakawaua katikati yake.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo waliwakimbia watu wa Israeli kuelekea jangwani. Lakini hawakuweza kuyaepuka mapigano. Askari wa Israeli walitoka mijini, wakawaua pale kati ya majeshi mawili.

es.L: Y se volvieron delante de los hombres de Israel hacia el camino del desierto, pero la batalla los alcanzó, y los que [venían] de las ciudades los destruían en medio de ella.
es.B: Así que dieron la vuelta y huyeron de los hombres de Israel hacia el desierto, pero no pudieron escapar de la lucha, y los que salían de las ciudades los abatían en medio de ella.
es.R: Así que huyeron de los hombres de Israel hacia el desierto. Pero no pudieron escapar de la batalla. Los soldados israelitas salieron de los pueblos y los mataron allí, entre los dos ejércitos.

decisions.choice: the battle overtook them: they could not get away from the fighting
decisions.reason: The battle is pictured as chasing and catching them. They fled, but the fighting came after them.

decisions.choice: those from the cities destroying them in its midst: the Hebrew is hard to follow
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the cities", plural, and "in its midst". It most likely means the men of the ambush, coming out of Gibeah and other towns, caught the Benjaminites between them and the main army. A reading "the city", meaning Gibeah alone, would be smoother, but the Hebrew text has the plural.

decisions.choice: toward the wilderness: east, to the dry country toward the Jordan
decisions.reason: The wilderness here is the dry, rocky land east of Benjamin's towns, sloping down to the Jordan valley. It is where the survivors flee (verse 45).

decisions.choice: Israelite soldiers ... between the two armies
decisions.reason: Readable says who came out of the towns and what "in its midst" means (m2).

source.text: כִּתְּר֤וּ אֶת־בִּנְיָמִן֙ הִרְדִיפֻ֔הוּ מְנוּחָ֖ה הִדְרִיכֻ֑הוּ עַ֛ד נֹ֥כַח הַגִּבְעָ֖ה מִמִּזְרַח־שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: They surrounded Benjamin, they pursued him; [at] resting place they trod him down, as far as opposite the Gibeah from [the] rising of [the] sun.

en.L: They surrounded Benjamin, they pursued him; [at] Menuhah they trod him down, as far as opposite Gibeah toward the rising of the sun.
en.B: They surrounded the Benjaminites and chased them, and they trampled them down at Menuhah, as far as the area east of Gibeah.
en.R: They surrounded the men of Benjamin and chased them. They crushed them at a place called Menuhah, as far as the area east of Gibeah.

sw.L: Wakamzunguka Benyamini, wakamfuatia; [huko] Menuha wakamkanyaga, mpaka mkabala na Gibea upande wa mawio ya jua.
sw.B: Waliwazunguka Wabenyamini, wakawafukuza, wakawakanyaga huko Menuha, mpaka eneo la mashariki ya Gibea.
sw.R: Waliwazunguka watu wa Benyamini, wakawafukuza. Waliwaponda mahali paitwapo Menuha, mpaka eneo la mashariki ya Gibea.

es.L: Rodearon a Benjamín, lo persiguieron; [en] Menúha lo pisotearon, hasta frente a Guibeá, hacia donde sale el sol.
es.B: Rodearon a los benjamitas y los persiguieron, y los aplastaron en Menúha, hasta la zona al este de Guibeá.
es.R: Rodearon a los hombres de Benjamín y los persiguieron. Los aplastaron en un lugar llamado Menúha, hasta la zona al este de Guibeá.

decisions.choice: Menuhah: most likely a place name; it can also mean "rest" or "easily"
decisions.reason: The word means "rest" or "resting place". It may name a place, perhaps the clan town of Nohah in Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:2). It may also mean they trampled them down "at their resting place", where they stopped, or "without effort". Some copies of the Greek translation read it as the place name Nohah.

decisions.choice: surrounded, pursued, trod down: three verbs without "and"
decisions.reason: The verbs are set side by side with no joining word, which makes the account quick and breathless.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun: on the east
decisions.reason: "The rising of the sun" means the east.

decisions.choice: at Menuhah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the word as a place name (m1); Literal brackets "at" since the Hebrew has no preposition.

source.text: וַֽיִּפְּלוּ֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן שְׁמֹנָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה אַנְשֵׁי־חָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand man; all these [were] men of strength.

en.L: And there fell of Benjamin 18,000 men; all these [were] men of strength.
en.B: Of Benjamin 18,000 men fell, all of them brave warriors.
en.R: Of Benjamin's army 18,000 men were killed. All of them were brave soldiers.

sw.L: Na wakaanguka katika Benyamini watu 18,000; hawa wote [walikuwa] watu hodari.
sw.B: Kwa upande wa Benyamini walianguka watu 18,000, wote wakiwa mashujaa hodari.
sw.R: Katika jeshi la Benyamini waliuawa watu 18,000. Wote walikuwa askari hodari.

es.L: Y cayeron de Benjamín 18 000 hombres; todos estos [eran] hombres valientes.
es.B: De Benjamín cayeron 18 000 hombres, todos ellos guerreros valientes.
es.R: Del ejército de Benjamín murieron 18 000 hombres. Todos eran soldados valientes.

decisions.choice: men of strength: able, brave warriors
decisions.reason: The phrase names men of strength, skill and courage in war (6:12; 11:1). It honors the fallen Benjaminites even in defeat.

decisions.choice: 18,000: the first part of the total
decisions.reason: Verses 44-45 add up to 25,000: 18,000 here, then 5,000 and 2,000 (verse 45), the round number of verse 46. On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

source.text: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ וַיָּנֻ֤סוּ הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ אֶל־סֶ֣לַע הָֽרִמּ֔וֹן וַיְעֹֽלְלֻ֨הוּ֙ בַּֽמְסִלּ֔וֹת חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּדְבִּ֤יקוּ אַחֲרָיו֙ עַד־גִּדְעֹ֔ם וַיַּכּ֥וּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ אַלְפַּ֥יִם אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned and fled to the wilderness, to [the] rock of the Rimmon. And they gleaned him on the highways, five thousand man; and they pursued closely after him to Gidom and they struck of him two thousand man.

en.L: And they turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. And they gleaned them on the highways, 5,000 men, and they pursued hard after them as far as Gidom and struck 2,000 men of them.
en.B: Then they turned and ran toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites picked off 5,000 men along the roads, and they kept after them as far as Gidom and killed 2,000 more.
en.R: The rest of Benjamin's men ran toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites hunted down and killed 5,000 of them along the roads. They chased them as far as Gidom and killed 2,000 more.

sw.L: Nao wakageuka, wakakimbia kuelekea nyika, mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni. Nao wakawaokota katika njia kuu, watu 5,000, wakawafuatia kwa karibu mpaka Gidomu, wakawapiga watu 2,000 kati yao.
sw.B: Kisha waligeuka wakakimbia kuelekea nyikani, mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni. Waisraeli waliwaua mmoja mmoja watu 5,000 katika njia kuu, wakaendelea kuwafuatia mpaka Gidomu, wakaua wengine 2,000.
sw.R: Watu wa Benyamini waliobaki walikimbia kuelekea jangwani, mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni. Waisraeli waliwasaka na kuwaua 5,000 kati yao kando ya njia. Waliwafukuza mpaka Gidomu, wakaua wengine 2,000.

es.L: Y se volvieron y huyeron hacia el desierto, a la peña de Rimón. Y los rebuscaron en los caminos, 5000 hombres, y los persiguieron de cerca hasta Gidom e hirieron de ellos a 2000 hombres.
es.B: Entonces dieron la vuelta y huyeron hacia el desierto, a la peña de Rimón. Los israelitas cazaron a 5000 hombres por los caminos, y los siguieron de cerca hasta Gidom y mataron a 2000 más.
es.R: Los demás hombres de Benjamín huyeron hacia el desierto, a la peña de Rimón. Los israelitas persiguieron y mataron a 5000 de ellos por los caminos. Los persiguieron hasta Gidom y mataron a 2000 más.

decisions.choice: gleaned them: picked them off one by one
decisions.reason: Gleaning is gathering the grain or grapes left after the harvest (Leviticus 19:9-10; 8:2). The picture is of the tribes catching the stragglers, the last ones left, along the roads.

decisions.choice: the rock of Rimmon; Gidom: places east of Gibeah
decisions.reason: The rock of Rimmon was a high crag or cliff, most likely near the town of Rimmon east of Bethel, a hard place to attack. Gidom is not known today.

decisions.choice: The Israelites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they"; Balanced and Readable say who did the killing, since the subject changes from Benjamin to Israel.

decisions.choice: "los rebuscaron" (L); "cazaron" (B); "persiguieron y mataron" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of gleaning, picking up what is left after the harvest (m1), with "rebuscar", the Spanish word for that; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כָל־הַנֹּ֨פְלִ֜ים מִבִּנְיָמִ֗ן עֶשְׂרִים֩ וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה אֶ֥לֶף אִ֛ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חֶ֖רֶב בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֶֽת־כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה אַנְשֵׁי־חָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And were all those fallen of Benjamin twenty and five thousand man drawing [the] sword on the day the that; all these [were] men of strength.

en.L: And all who fell of Benjamin were 25,000 men drawing [the] sword on that day; all these [were] men of strength.
en.B: So in all 25,000 men of Benjamin who were armed with swords fell that day, all of them brave warriors.
en.R: That day 25,000 of Benjamin's soldiers were killed. All of them were brave men who fought with swords.

sw.L: Na wote walioanguka wa Benyamini walikuwa watu 25,000 wenye kufuta upanga siku hiyo; hawa wote [walikuwa] watu hodari.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo jumla ya watu wa Benyamini wenye panga walioanguka siku hiyo walikuwa 25,000, wote wakiwa mashujaa hodari.
sw.R: Siku hiyo askari 25,000 wa Benyamini waliuawa. Wote walikuwa watu hodari waliopigana kwa panga.

es.L: Y todos los que cayeron de Benjamín fueron 25 000 hombres que sacaban espada, aquel día; todos estos [eran] hombres valientes.
es.B: Así que en total cayeron aquel día 25 000 hombres de Benjamín armados de espada, todos ellos guerreros valientes.
es.R: Aquel día murieron 25 000 soldados de Benjamín. Todos eran hombres valientes que peleaban con espada.

decisions.choice: 25,000: the round total of verse 35's 25,100
decisions.reason: Verse 35 gives the exact number, 25,100; this verse rounds it, as the sum of verses 44-45 (18,000, 5,000, 2,000) does. On the size of the numbers see verse 2.

decisions.choice: men of strength
decisions.reason: As in verse 44.

decisions.choice: drawing [the] sword (L); armed with swords (B); who fought with swords (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

source.text: וַיִּפְנ֞וּ וַיָּנֻ֤סוּ הַמִּדְבָּ֨רָה֙ אֶל־סֶ֣לַע הָֽרִמּ֔וֹן שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּסֶ֣לַע רִמּ֔וֹן אַרְבָּעָ֖ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned and fled to the wilderness, to [the] rock of the Rimmon, six hundred man, and they stayed at [the] rock of Rimmon four months.

en.L: But 600 men turned and fled toward the wilderness, to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon four months.
en.B: But 600 men turned and escaped into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they stayed there four months.
en.R: But 600 men escaped into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. They stayed there for four months.

sw.L: Lakini watu 600 wakageuka, wakakimbia kuelekea nyika, mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni, nao wakakaa katika mwamba wa Rimoni miezi minne.
sw.B: Lakini watu 600 waligeuka wakakimbilia nyikani mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni, nao wakakaa huko miezi minne.
sw.R: Lakini watu 600 walikimbilia jangwani mpaka mwamba wa Rimoni. Walikaa huko kwa miezi minne.

es.L: Pero se volvieron y huyeron hacia el desierto, a la peña de Rimón, 600 hombres, y se quedaron en la peña de Rimón cuatro meses.
es.B: Pero 600 hombres dieron la vuelta y escaparon al desierto, a la peña de Rimón, y se quedaron allí cuatro meses.
es.R: Pero 600 hombres escaparon al desierto, a la peña de Rimón. Se quedaron allí cuatro meses.

decisions.choice: 600 men: all that was left of Benjamin
decisions.reason: These 600 are the tribe's only survivors. Chapter 21 tells how the tribes, grieving that one tribe was about to be lost, found wives for them (21:6-7, 13).

decisions.choice: they stayed at the rock four months: a stronghold that could not easily be taken
decisions.reason: The crag gave the survivors a safe place to hold out until the tribes sent word of peace to them (21:13).

decisions.choice: there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "there" for the second "rock of Rimmon"; Literal repeats the name as the Hebrew does.

source.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל שָׁ֣בוּ אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּם לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב מֵעִ֤יר מְתֹם֙ עַד־בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַ֖ד כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֑א גַּ֛ם כָּל־הֶעָרִ֥ים הַנִּמְצָא֖וֹת שִׁלְּח֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] men of Israel turned back to [the] sons of Benjamin, and struck them to [the] mouth of [the] sword, from [the] city, entire, to [the] beast, to all that was found; also all the cities that were found they sent in the fire.

en.L: And the men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the entire city to the beasts, to everything that was found; also all the cities that were found they set on fire.
en.B: Then the men of Israel turned back against the Benjaminites and struck them down with the sword, from the people of the towns to the animals, everything they found. They also set on fire every town they came to.
en.R: Then the men of Israel went back to the towns of Benjamin. They killed the people and the animals, everything they found. They burned every town they came to.

sw.L: Nao watu wa Israeli wakawarudia wana wa Benyamini, wakawapiga kwa makali ya upanga, kuanzia mji mzima mpaka wanyama, mpaka kila kitu kilichoonekana; tena miji yote iliyoonekana wakaitia moto.
sw.B: Kisha watu wa Israeli waliwarudia Wabenyamini, wakawaua kwa upanga, kuanzia watu wa miji mpaka wanyama, kila kitu walichokikuta. Pia waliichoma moto kila mji waliofika.
sw.R: Kisha watu wa Israeli walirudi katika miji ya Benyamini. Waliwaua watu na wanyama, kila kitu walichokikuta. Waliichoma moto kila mji waliofika.

es.L: Y los hombres de Israel se volvieron contra los hijos de Benjamín y los hirieron a filo de espada, desde la ciudad entera hasta el ganado, hasta todo lo que se hallaba; también prendieron fuego a todas las ciudades que se hallaban.
es.B: Después los hombres de Israel se volvieron contra los benjamitas y los hirieron a espada, desde la gente de las ciudades hasta el ganado, todo lo que encontraron. También prendieron fuego a todas las ciudades que hallaron.
es.R: Después los hombres de Israel volvieron a los pueblos de Benjamín. Mataron a la gente y a los animales, todo lo que encontraron. Quemaron todos los pueblos que encontraron.

decisions.choice: the entire city: the Hebrew text; some copies read "the men of the city"
alternatives: from the men of the city to the beasts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means "soundness" or "entire", giving "from the entire city". A few Hebrew copies have a word that differs by one vowel and means "men", giving "from the men of the city to the beasts", which fits the list better. The meaning is much the same: everyone in the towns.

decisions.choice: they struck ... and set the cities on fire: Benjamin treated like a town devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: The tribes do to Benjamin's towns what the law commands for a town in Israel that serves other gods: kill its people and animals with the sword and burn it (Deuteronomy 13:16-17). The story tells it without approval; chapter 21 shows the tribes grieving over what they had done (21:2-3, 6, 15).

decisions.choice: struck them with the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: As at verse 37 and 1:8: they killed them.

decisions.choice: from the people of the towns to the animals (B); the people and the animals (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom the word "city" stands for here: everyone in the towns (m1).
